stories.headline: The End of the App: Why Conversational Interfaces Are Replacing Screens
stories.dek: As voice and agent-driven interaction matures, the traditional screen-based app paradigm is being challenged. Designers now must think in flows, not frames — and the shift is bigger than mobile-to-web ever was.

stories.headline: Designing for Uncertainty: How to Build Products That Survive Rapid AI Change
stories.dek: The best product teams in 2026 are designing for optionality — building modular systems that can absorb AI capability upgrades without requiring full redesigns.

stories.headline: Micro-Feedback Loops: The Design Pattern Every AI Product Needs
stories.dek: Lightweight in-context feedback — a thumbs up, a quick correction, a tone dial — is how leading AI products improve without breaking the flow. Here's how to design them well.

stories.headline: The Comeback of Skeuomorphism — But Make It AI
stories.dek: Flat design's reign may be ending. As AI interfaces try to signal capability and trustworthiness, designers are reaching back to tactile metaphors — but with a modern, data-driven twist.

stories.headline: Shadow AI Use in Enterprise: What Researchers Are Finding When They Actually Look
stories.dek: New field studies show employees use personal AI tools for work tasks at rates companies never suspected — creating invisible UX gaps and compliance exposure that research teams are just beginning to map.

stories.headline: Diary Studies Are Having a Moment — Here's Why Longitudinal UX Is Back
stories.dek: With AI products embedding into daily routines, snapshot usability tests are missing the full picture. Diary studies that track behavior over weeks are back in fashion — and much cheaper to run in 2026.

stories.headline: How to Run AI-Assisted Thematic Analysis Without Losing the Human Signal
stories.dek: AI can cluster 500 interview transcripts in minutes — but researchers warn that automated theme labeling flattens nuance. A new protocol from Spotify's research team aims to preserve it.

stories.headline: The Curse of the Expert Researcher: Why Deep UX Knowledge Slows Insight Cycles
stories.dek: Experienced researchers often take longer to synthesize findings than generalists with AI tools. A provocative new analysis suggests the field needs to rethink seniority ladders and what 'expertise' actually means now.

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude for Work: Shared Memory, Team Projects, Persistent Context
stories.dek: Claude for Work introduces org-level memory and shared project spaces, letting teams build a persistent institutional knowledge layer that every Claude conversation can draw from automatically.

stories.headline: Figma AI Adds 'Design from Brief' — One Prompt, Full Component Set
stories.dek: Figma's April update introduces end-to-end brief-to-component generation: paste a product requirement and get a responsive component set, annotated and variant-ready, in seconds.

stories.headline: Perplexity Launches Comet: An AI Browser That Reasons Before It Browses
stories.dek: Comet replaces the traditional address bar with a reasoning layer — the browser plans a multi-step research path before fetching any pages, returning synthesized answers rather than raw results.

stories.headline: NotebookLM Adds Live Collaboration: Multiple Researchers, One Shared AI Mind
stories.dek: Google's NotebookLM now supports real-time multiplayer sessions where up to 20 researchers can simultaneously interrogate the same document set, see each other's queries, and build shared insight threads.

stories.headline: OpenAI Releases o4: Reasoning Model That Plans, Searches, and Self-Corrects Mid-Task
stories.dek: o4 introduces continuous self-evaluation during long tasks — the model pauses, audits its own reasoning chain, and backtracks when it detects likely errors, dramatically reducing hallucination rates on complex tasks.

stories.headline: DeepMind's AlphaFold 4 Predicts Protein-Drug Binding With Near-Lab Accuracy
stories.dek: The latest AlphaFold release extends beyond protein structure prediction into binding affinity modeling, giving drug discovery teams a computational alternative to expensive wet-lab screening at the early discovery stage.

stories.headline: The Alignment Tax Is Shrinking: Safe Models Now Within 3% of Unconstrained Benchmarks
stories.dek: A new Stanford analysis shows that the performance gap between safety-aligned and unconstrained frontier models has narrowed to 3% on standard reasoning tasks — a milestone for making alignment economically viable.

stories.headline: Mixture-of-Experts Goes Consumer: Why Your Next Phone Will Run a 70B-Class Model
stories.dek: New MoE architectures activate only a fraction of parameters per inference step, making models that rival GPT-4-class performance runnable on smartphone hardware — with no cloud dependency.

stories.headline: RISC-V Hits Critical Mass: 50% of New IoT SoC Designs Now Use Open ISA
stories.dek: For the first time, RISC-V has crossed the majority threshold in new IoT chip designs, according to an RISC-V International survey — driven by licensing costs, customisation freedom, and growing toolchain maturity.

stories.headline: Ambient Backscatter 2.0: IoT Sensors That Harvest Wi-Fi Signals to Run Indefinitely
stories.dek: A University of Washington team demonstrated a new ambient backscatter protocol that harvests enough energy from ambient Wi-Fi and Bluetooth signals to run a full BLE sensor node perpetually — with no battery.

stories.headline: Matter 2.0 Ratified: Thread Mesh, Energy Reporting, and Camera APIs Now Standard
stories.dek: The Connectivity Standards Alliance ratified Matter 2.0, adding Thread mesh networking, standardised energy-usage reporting for appliances, and a unified camera streaming API — closing major gaps that slowed smart home adoption.

stories.headline: Industrial IoT Security: Why OT Networks Are Still the Weakest Link in 2026
stories.dek: A new Dragos threat report finds that 68% of critical-infrastructure incidents start with an unsecured OT device — and that patching cycles measured in years, not weeks, remain the core systemic problem.

stories.headline: NVIDIA Jetson Thor Lands: 2,000 TOPS, Designed for Humanoid Robots and Autonomous Vehicles
stories.dek: Jetson Thor is NVIDIA's most powerful edge AI module to date, targeting applications that require full autonomy — from warehouse robots to autonomous delivery vehicles — all running locally with no cloud dependency.

stories.headline: Federated Learning Reaches Production Scale in Manufacturing AIoT Deployments
stories.dek: Siemens and Bosch have both shipped production federated-learning pipelines where hundreds of factory-floor AIoT devices train a shared quality-control model without sharing raw sensor data — addressing privacy and bandwidth constraints simultaneously.

stories.headline: TinyML Benchmarks 2026: Which Edge AI Frameworks Win on Power vs. Accuracy?
stories.dek: An independent benchmark comparing TensorFlow Lite, ONNX Runtime, and ExecuTorch on six hardware platforms reveals wide divergence in power draw — and that the 'best' framework depends entirely on your target chip.

stories.headline: Smart Grid Meets AIoT: How Utilities Are Using Edge AI to Prevent Blackouts
stories.dek: Pacific Gas & Electric deployed an AIoT sensor grid across 1,200 substations that predicts equipment failure 72 hours in advance — the pilot prevented an estimated 14 outages in its first six months.

stories.headline: John Deere's Autonomous Tractor Logs 1 Million Hours: What the Data Shows
stories.dek: John Deere released a first-of-kind operational dataset from its autonomous tractor fleet — revealing that machine-hours per acre have dropped 34%, while fuel efficiency improved 18% compared to human-operated baselines.

stories.headline: Vertical Farming's Profitability Crisis — and How AI Is the Only Path Out
stories.dek: After a wave of closures, the surviving vertical farms share one thing: AI-optimized grow cycles. The technology has cut energy-per-kilogram by up to 40%, finally making the economics work for leafy greens at scale.

stories.headline: EU Approves 'Digital Farm Twin' Subsidy — €2B to Connect Every EU Farm by 2030
stories.dek: The European Commission approved a landmark programme funding digital twin infrastructure for EU farms, linking soil sensors, satellite imagery, and weather data into unified farm-management platforms for operators of all scales.

stories.headline: Barcelona's Tech Hiring Surge: 40% More Senior Design Roles Than This Time Last Year
stories.dek: LinkedIn Talent Insights data shows Barcelona posted 40% more senior product design and UX roles in Q1 2026 versus Q1 2025, with the strongest demand coming from fintech, health-tech, and B2B SaaS scale-ups.

stories.headline: The €90K Design Role: Why Barcelona Salaries Are Catching Up to London and Amsterdam
stories.dek: A new Levels.fyi analysis shows Barcelona senior designer salaries now reaching €85–95K total compensation at scale-ups — still a gap to London, but narrowing as remote-first culture reduces geographic arbitrage.

stories.headline: Wallapop, Holaluz, and Factorial Open Design System Roles — April 2026 Roundup
stories.dek: Three prominent Barcelona tech companies posted design system and principal design roles this week, signalling continued investment in foundational design infrastructure rather than feature-team headcount alone.

stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV Elected: First American Pope in Catholic Church History
stories.dek: Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost of Chicago was elected Pope Leo XIV on Thursday, becoming the first American to lead the Catholic Church. The 69-year-old is known for his work with marginalised communities and his moderate theological stance.

stories.headline: Trump Signs Executive Order Directing Treasury to Explore Sovereign Wealth Fund
stories.dek: A new executive order instructs the Treasury and Commerce departments to present a plan within 90 days for establishing a US sovereign wealth fund — drawing comparisons to Norway's $1.7 trillion oil fund.

stories.headline: Record Heat in South Asia: India and Pakistan Hit 51°C as Monsoon Delays Worsen
stories.dek: Unprecedented April temperatures across India and Pakistan — including a 51°C reading in Jacobabad — are straining power grids and accelerating calls for emergency climate-adaptation funding ahead of a delayed monsoon season.
